question.problem: Suppose that $A$ and $B$ are two events such that $P(A)=0.6,$ $P(B)=0.5,$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.7,$ find $P(A\cap B).$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14284903/assets/01f86c8b4dc5c77efefba2e652c69cf3c6c4e42a25830ad2abbb78b6ca5d81bc.png)

The addition law for probability states that

$$
P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B).
$$

So, to calculate $P(A\cap B),$ we apply the addition law:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A\cup B) & =P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B) \\ 0.7 & =0.6+0.5-P(A\cap B) \\ P(A\cap B) & =0.6+0.5-0.7 \\ P(A\cap B) & =0.4\end{aligned}
$$
